name: Pyrenees
description: Mountain region where villages have specialist huntsmen who sell game on the open market.

name: Germany
description: Region whose forests host village huntsmen; German draught horse breeds are notable.

name: Angevin Domains
description: Lands where feudal grants of exclusive hunting rights (warrens and chases) are customary.

name: England
description: Kingdom where a third of the land was designated royal forest under King John; home of horse coursers and fine rounceys.

name: France
description: Kingdom where exclusive hunting grants are customary and the heartland of the tournament.

name: Royal Forest of Dartmoor
description: An English royal forest composed of moorland, showing that a 'forest' is a hunting reserve rather than woodland.

name: St. Hubert Monastery
description: Swiss monastery whose abbot breeds the St. Hubert running hounds, famed for their noses.

name: Scotland
description: Source of the best greyhounds; northern ponies are also found there.

name: Ireland
description: Home of the shaggy-coated wolfhound; produces fine rounceys.

name: Iberia
description: Source of the best bird dogs (spaniels) and of most destriers; horse dealers are respected there.

name: Andalusia
description: Region of Iberia from which many destrier stallions come.

name: Scandinavia
description: Northern lands where hunters pursue reindeer and gyrfalcons live; produces fine rounceys.

name: Novgorod
description: Eastern region where hunting with hounds is part of noble culture and horse dealers are disreputable.

name: The Levant
description: Region where horse dealing is respected, mares are used as warhorses, and small tournaments are held near towns.

name: North Africa
description: Source of Barb horses and of the lanner falcon.

name: Iceland
description: Source of the very best working ponies and home of gyrfalcons.

name: Hungary
description: Kingdom known for the quality of its riding horses such as palfreys and jennets.

name: Low Countries
description: Region producing good draught horses.

name: Russia
description: Cold northern land where the gyrfalcon lives.

name: Sicily
description: The court of Sicily originated the fashion of hooding hawks.

name: Provence
description: Region where fin' amors (courtly love) originated.

name: Burgundy
description: Region where fin' amors (courtly love) originated.

name: Lagny-sur-Marne
description: Site of the 1179 tourney to which Henry the Young King brought five hundred knights.

name: Lincoln
description: Site relieved in 1217 by William Marshal, leading to the expulsion of Louis of France.

name: Flanders
description: County of Count Philip, whose side William Marshal joined on the tournament circuit.

name: Pembrokeshire
description: Earldom held by William Marshal.

name: Holy Land
description: Tournaments are held wherever European knights are found, including the Holy Land.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The Ars Magica setting, in which hunting, horses, hawking and tournaments are central noble pursuits.

name: Loch Leglean Tribunal
description: Tribunal where bow and stable hunting is a socially acceptable noble pursuit.

name: Hibernian Tribunal
description: Tribunal where bow and stable hunting is a socially acceptable noble pursuit.

name: Stonehenge Tribunal
description: Tribunal where bow and stable hunting is a socially acceptable noble pursuit.

name: Iberian Tribunal
description: Tribunal where bow and stable hunting is acceptable and where courtly love is widely known.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Tribunal where bow and stable hunting is acceptable and where courtly love is widely known.

name: Novgorod Tribunal
description: Tribunal where bow and stable hunting is acceptable; it produces good draught horses.

name: Roman Tribunal
description: Tribunal region where fin' amors is now widely known.

name: King John
description: King of England during whose reign a third of the nation was designated forest; died in 1216.

name: William Rufus
description: King of England killed in August 1100 by an arrow accidentally shot by William Tyrell while hunting.

name: William Tyrell
description: Man who accidentally shot King William Rufus in 1100.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
description: Popularized fin' amors, spreading it to England and France.

name: Andreas Capellanus
description: Author in 1174 of De Amore, the definitive work on fin' amors, listing 12 Laws of Love.

name: Tristan
description: Lover in the romance of Tristan and Iseult, whose adultery brings disaster.

name: Iseult
description: Lover in the romance of Tristan and Iseult.

name: Henry II
description: King of England who banned tournaments and charged William Marshal with tutoring his son.

name: King Richard
description: King of England who allowed tournaments again in 1194 under royal charters.

name: Henry III
description: King of England in 1220; William Marshal was elected his regent in 1216.

name: Henry the Young King
description: Son of Henry II, who took five hundred knights to Lagny-sur-Marne in 1179 and was tutored by William Marshal.

name: William Marshal
description: Great knight and Earl of Pembrokeshire who rose through tournaments, served successive kings and was regent for Henry III; died 1219.

name: Roger de Jouy
description: Flemish knight who shared tournament ransom profits with William Marshal for a year.

name: William de Tancarville
description: Influential Norman noble, cousin of William Marshal's father, who introduced him to the tournament.

name: Count Philip of Flanders
description: Noble whose wealth lured William Marshal to his side on the tournament circuit.

name: Louis of France
description: French prince expelled from England after the relief of Lincoln in 1217.

name: Jonathan Carpenter
description: Example character who gains the Reputation Patron (Clergy) by building a nave for a parish church.

name: House Verditius
description: Hermetic House whose magi send agents to tournaments to sell minor enchantments to knights.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of magi; acting as its patron is fraught with difficulty, and it is one of the Reputation groups.

name: The Church
description: Major landholder that condemns fin' amors and tournaments and can grant Gratitude and manors.

name: Troubadours
description: Singers who celebrate fin' amors and can glorify a patron's genealogy.

name: Master of Kennels
description: Skilled commoner professional who trains and manages a noble's hounds and organizes the huntsmen.

name: Huntsman
description: Dog handler who seeks out prey with lymers during the quest and positions hounds in the relay; grogs perform the role well.

name: Falconer
description: Professional who trains hawks and falcons for a noble.

name: Austringer
description: A specialist falconer who trains non-falcons such as hawks.

name: Marshal
description: Specialist who coordinates the care of horses in superior stables; the Marshal of England commands the king's cavalry.

name: Herald
description: Tournament official who publicizes events, knows knights' devices, provides commentary and adjudicates.

name: Knight
description: Mounted noble warrior for whom the tournament is practice for war and a source of ransom.

name: Errant Knight
description: Knight who makes his living from the tournament circuit rather than a fief.

name: Grog
description: Covenant servant; grogs make admirable huntsmen.

name: Magus
description: Hermetic magician; magi may be troubled by hunts or secretly sponsor tournament teams.

name: Quaesitor
description: Hermetic investigator to whom a Verditius complains about illegal sales of enchanted devices.

name: Horse Courser
description: English term for a horse dealer, a profession with a bad reputation.

name: Poacher
description: Illegal hunter on reserved land, sometimes of noble or clerical rank, fiercely punished.

name: Farrier
description: Maker of horseshoes, overseen by a marshal.

name: Master of Kennels (Virtue)
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for a character managing a noble's kennels; grants 50 extra experience points in related Abilities.

name: Falconer (Virtue)
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for a character training hawks and falcons for a noble patron; grants 50 extra experience points.

name: Marshal (Virtue)
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for the specialist in charge of a noble's stables; grants 50 extra experience points.

name: Ferocity
description: Virtue possessed by alaunts, mastiffs, warhorses and gyrfalcons in specific circumstances.

name: Improved Characteristics
description: Virtue possessed by horse templates such as the destrier and courser.

name: Long-Winded
description: Virtue found on the horse templates.

name: Perfect Balance
description: Virtue representing working ponies' sure-footedness on treacherous mountain paths.

name: Keen Vision
description: Virtue possessed by the gyrfalcon.

name: Educated
description: Virtue many falconers possess.

name: Landed Noble
description: Social Status Virtue for a knight holding at least a single manor.

name: Great Noble
description: Social Status Virtue for a character whose land is so large it requires infeudation.

name: Wealthy
description: Virtue making a character rich relative to his social class; wealthy knights need tourney only one season a year.

name: True Love
description: A character with this Virtue may not be caught up in romance except with its object.

name: Proud
description: Flaw (minor) found on warhorses and gained by rounceys.

name: Noncombatant
description: Flaw on draught horses and working ponies.

name: Fragile Constitution
description: Flaw possessed by the gyrfalcon.

name: Poor
description: Flaw making a character poor for his class; poor knights must tourney three seasons a year.

name: Lost Love
description: A character with this Flaw may not become involved in other romances.

name: Hunt
description: Ability used to track, assess and pursue prey and to follow hunting customs.

name: Animal Handling
description: Ability used to tame, command and train animals, including hawks and hounds.

name: Etiquette
description: Ability governing knowledge of the accepted format of noble hunting.

name: Area Lore
description: Ability essential for understanding terrain when positioning the relay and reducing the Terrain Bonus.

name: Ride
description: Ability tested heavily during the chase.

name: Athletics
description: Ability used by hounds and prey during the chase.

name: Awareness
description: Ability possessed by hounds, horses and birds in their templates.

name: Brawl
description: Ability used by animals for bites and hooves.

name: Stealth
description: Ability of lymers and peregrine falcons.

name: Survival
description: Ability of the gyrfalcon in cold climates.

name: Leadership
description: Ability of pack leaders and lanners enabling group attacks.

name: Profession: Master of Kennels
description: Ability governing the care, breeding and treatment of hounds; required for kennel Living Conditions bonuses.

name: Profession: Marshal
description: Ability for understanding, purchasing and caring for horses; functions as Medicine for animals.

name: Profession: Falconer
description: Ability governing care, breeding and acquisition of hawks and falcons.

name: Profession: Herald
description: Ability to recognize knights by device, recall their deeds, adjudicate tournament law and locate tournaments.

name: Intrigue
description: Ability used to arrange romantic meetings and understand the politics of patronage.

name: Charm
description: Ability that is the primary means of pursuing a lady in fin' amors.

name: Latin
description: Ability among those favored by master of kennels, falconer and marshal Virtues.

name: Medicine
description: Ability that Profession Marshal substitutes for in treating animal diseases.

name: Single Weapon
description: Combat Ability used to compute a knight's tournament Labor Points.

name: Great Weapon
description: Combat Ability used to compute a knight's tournament Labor Points.

name: Martial Abilities
description: Category of Abilities that masters of kennels and marshals may take freely.

name: Magic Realm
description: Realm to which some destriers and faerie/magical horses are aligned.

name: Faerie Realm
description: Realm of faeries, who may offer knights arms or horses with unusual powers.

name: Divine Realm
description: Realm invoked at tournaments through patron saints; Divine horses exist.

name: Infernal Realm
description: Realm of diabolic forces offering bargains at tournaments; Infernal horses exist.

name: Lymer
description: Heavy-jowled scent hound related to the bloodhound, trained to track silently.

name: Running Dog
description: Pack hound that pursues prey in pairs by scent, resembling the foxhound.

name: St. Hubert Hound
description: The best breed of running dog, bred by the abbot of St. Hubert; slow but with unrivaled nose.

name: Greyhound
description: Fast sight hound used to catch and bring down prey; the best come from Scotland.

name: Wolfhound
description: Shaggy-coated Irish hound performing the same role as the greyhound.

name: Alaunt
description: Powerful fighting hound (Great Dane) brought forward for the final kill.

name: Mastiff
description: Shaggy, vicious guard and hunting dog used against boar or bear.

name: Harrier
description: Small dog used to chase hares in bow and stable hunting.

name: Bird Dog
description: Dog trained for hawking; the best come from Iberia and are called espagnols or spaniels.

name: Unicorn
description: Magical beast almost impossible to catch; hunting one brings Reputation.

name: Hart
description: Stag, the object of most hunts, hunted in spring and summer.

name: Boar
description: Malicious, dangerous prey hunted from midsummer through autumn with a boar spear.

name: Bear
description: Dangerous prey with great stamina, hunted in all seasons except spring.

name: Hare
description: Safe prey, better pursued by sighthounds; also hawking prey.

name: Wolf
description: Feared predator whose hunting is a necessity rather than an honor.

name: Fox
description: Cunning prey that gives good sport but little prestige.

name: Otter
description: Riverine predator hunted with disdain in summer or autumn.

name: Reindeer
description: Fabled Scandinavian prey said to give good sport.

name: Fallow Deer
description: Rare deer.

name: Roe Deer
description: Deer considered too small for serious attention.

name: Destrier
description: Noble warhorse of the highest status, often Spanish and often aligned with a realm.

name: Courser
description: The most common combat-trained warhorse.

name: Rouncey
description: Utility horse with courser combat training, favored by squires.

name: Palfrey
description: Standard riding horse for general use and travel.

name: Jennet
description: A palfrey ridden by a lady, always a mare.

name: Hackney
description: Draught horse used for farm work and pulling carts.

name: Working Pony
description: Sturdy pony (Fell or Icelandic) suited for rough terrain and as a pack animal.

name: Barb
description: Horse from North Africa, Muslim Iberia or the Levant that makes a fine courser or destrier.

name: Horse of Virtue
description: Exceptional horse; many destriers are Horses of Virtue.

name: Beast of Virtue
description: Exemplar of its kind possessing mythic powers; the best quarry after magical animals.

name: Hawk of Virtue
description: A finely trained Hawk of Virtue is a gift worthy of one's liege.

name: Falcon of Virtue
description: Rare falcon with burning feathers sought as a tournament prize in a story seed.

name: Gyrfalcon
description: Largest and most prized falcon, from cold northern lands; the base template for hawks and falcons.

name: Peregrine Falcon
description: Smaller ambush-predator falcon that attacks with a swooping dive.

name: Goshawk
description: Hawk flown from the fist, aggressive toward small prey.

name: Merlin
description: Small but very fast falcon for small prey.

name: Lanner
description: North African falcon easy to train and taught to hunt in pairs.

name: Sparrowhawk
description: Most common hawk in Mythic Europe, notoriously fragile.

name: Partridge
description: Game bird hunted by falcons.

name: Duck
description: Large bird brought down by paired hawks.

name: Goose
description: Prey animal; the largest prey a wild gyrfalcon can kill.

name: Pheasant
description: Typical hawking prey animal.

name: Heron
description: Typical hawking prey animal.

name: Crane
description: Large bird hunted by paired hawks.

name: Dragon
description: Magical beast one would not hunt with hounds.

name: Demon
description: A corrupting demon sponsors a silent tournament of undead knights in a story seed.

name: Faerie
description: Faeries seek out knights at tournaments to offer enchanted arms or horses, and transform hunters into beasts.

name: De Amore
description: Book by Andreas Capellanus (1174) setting the rules of fin' amors; full title Incipit liber amoris et curtesie.

name: Boar Spear
description: Special spear with a bar across the haft for boar hunting.

name: Jesses
description: Leather or silk cords securing a hawk to its perch.

name: Terret
description: Ring on a jess slipped over a perch or finger.

name: Creep
description: Great leather glove worn by a hawker.

name: Hawk Hood
description: Embroidered or bejeweled hood keeping a hawk calm, a fashion from the court of Sicily.

name: Horse Collar
description: New device allowing a horse to outperform an ox in draught work.

name: Tournament Enchantments
description: Minor enchantments sold by Verditius agents, such as reins that cannot be cut and saddles that grasp their rider.

name: Hunting
description: Prestigious noble sport governed by etiquette; nobles accept supernatural aid but not spells that ruin the sport.

name: Forest
description: Legal hunting reserve held by the king, not necessarily wooded.

name: Warren
description: Reserved hunting area granted to a noble or clergyman.

name: Hunting with Hounds
description: The most prestigious form of hunting: quest, assembly, relay, finding, chase, kill, and unmaking.

name: Bow and Stable Hunting
description: Driven hunt in which mounted hunters flush game toward a line of archers.

name: The Quest
description: Pre-dawn search for suitable prey by huntsmen with lymers.

name: The Assembly
description: Hunt breakfast where huntsmen present droppings and the prey is chosen.

name: The Relay
description: Positioning of fresh hounds along the prey's predicted route; can reduce the Terrain Bonus.

name: The Chase
description: Pursuit phase resolved by Pursuit Totals against Evasion Totals over rounds.

name: Unmaking
description: Butchering of the slain prey, followed by the curee, the rewarding of the dogs.

name: Pursuit Total
description: Hound Perception + Hunt + stress die minus fatigue, opposed to the prey's Evasion Total.

name: Evasion Total
description: Prey's Dexterity + Athletics + Terrain Bonus + stress die minus fatigue.

name: Terrain Bonus
description: +6 bonus to a native prey's Evasion Total, reduced by the relay and hunters.

name: Taming Creatures
description: Seasonal activity accumulating Intelligence + Animal Handling points to tame an animal.

name: Loyalty Test
description: Test of an animal's loyalty, subject to Gift penalties.

name: Aging Roll
description: Roll animals make seasonally once they reach a certain age.

name: Living Conditions Modifier
description: Modifier to aging granted by good kennels, stables or mews.

name: Confidence Score
description: Score of animals like alaunts and warhorses, used in taming totals.

name: Personality Traits
description: Traits such as Loyal, gained by tamed animals and patronage recipients.

name: Qualities
description: Creature Qualities such as Domesticated, Pursuit Predator and Fast Runner.

name: Pursuit Predator
description: Creature Quality of hounds and gyrfalcons.

name: Ambush Predator
description: Creature Quality of the peregrine falcon.

name: Might
description: Supernatural power rating that realm-aligned horses may possess.

name: The Gift
description: Magical talent whose social penalties apply to commanding animals and hawking.

name: Hawking
description: Falconry, a prestigious noble pursuit of hunting with trained birds of prey.

name: Establishment
description: Kennels, stables or mews with a quality, capacity, maintenance and Living Conditions modifier.

name: Kennels
description: Establishment for hounds whose size indicates noble prestige.

name: Mews
description: House for falcons and hawks.

name: Stables
description: Establishment for horses.

name: Fin' Amors
description: Courtly love: elaborate rules of romance between noble suitors and married ladies, condemned by the Church.

name: Twelve Laws of Love
description: Rules of love listed by Andreas Capellanus.

name: Patronage
description: Distribution of land, money, favors and titles, affecting Reputation and Gratitude.

name: Reputation
description: Measure of standing with a group such as Local, Clergy, Order of Hermes, Nobles, or Academics.

name: Prudhomme Reputation
description: Noble Reputation as an upstanding man, raised by tournaments and gifts.

name: Gratitude
description: Points earned by exceptional gifts or patronage, useful in future stories.

name: Tournament
description: Mock-war event of the 13th century offering experience, reputation, and ransom wealth.

name: Melee
description: Mock battle between two teams on the final day of a tournament.

name: Commencailles
description: Individual trials of sword and lance at vespers before the melee.

name: Regars
description: Review parade of both sides before the melee.

name: Estor
description: Signal to charge in the tournament melee.

name: Fiance
description: Submission of a defeated knight, securing a ransom.

name: Recets
description: Safe havens in the melee field where no fighting is allowed.

name: Lists
description: Hoardings marking starting points and site of jousting.

name: Bohort
description: Informal, impromptu tournament with blunted or wooden weapons.

name: Tirocinia
description: Tournaments for younger, less-experienced knights.

name: Joust
description: Contest of two knights charging with couched lances.

name: Grand Charge
description: The main melee charge, adjudicated by random encounters or mass combat.

name: Melee Events Table
description: Table of targets encountered in the melee, modified by Prudhomme Reputation.

name: Ransom
description: Payment (usually horse, armor or weapons) extracted from a surrendering knight.

name: Company
description: Group of knights riding under a single banner in tournaments, with its own Reputation.

name: Non-Lethal Combat
description: Optional combat rules used for bohorts and tournament melee.

name: Shock of the Charge
description: Optional combat rule used to resolve jousting.

name: Labor Points
description: Points describing business development, also applied to errant knights' tourney income.

name: Mythic Pound
description: Unit of account based on a pound of silver, divided into 20 shillings or 240 pence.

name: Knight Service
description: Military obligation owed on a manor, sometimes paid as scutage.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The Code, whose position on sponsoring knights or selling enchanted devices is questioned.

name: Covenant
description: Community of Hermetic magi that may be affected by hunts or seek tough men at tournaments.

name: Feudal System
description: Vassal-liege relationships of mutual obligation running through society.
